bastar-pine-project.whole: The World Bank's IDA lent US$4 million to the Madhya Pradesh Forestry Technical Assistance Project in Bastar (Lok Sabha answer, 1978). By the time it was written up in the Indian Forester (1982), it had planted 230 hectares of research trials and 1,356 hectares of pilot pine plantations, and the authors reported that growth data confirmed the pines grew fast. No figures on pulp supplied or costs were found, and no independent check of these figures was found.

pakistan-power-bills-2023.whole: The IMF's nine-month Stand-By Arrangement paid out about US$3 billion in total. At its final review in April 2024 the IMF said gross reserves had risen to around US$8 billion from US$4.5 billion at the start, that a primary budget surplus of 1.8% of GDP was reached in the first half of FY2024, and that inflation, 'while still elevated', was expected to fall to around 20% by end-June 2024, with growth of 2% expected. These are the IMF's own figures; no independent check was found.

bangladesh-fuel-strike-2013.whole: The three-year IMF Extended Credit Facility approved in April 2012 paid out SDR 639.96 million (about US$904 million). At its close in October 2015 the IMF said growth had been 'robust', inflation had eased and foreign exchange reserves had risen to 'a comfortable position', without giving figures. It also said Bangladesh's already low tax-to-GDP ratio had fallen steadily since 2012-13 and that energy subsidies still needed cutting. These are the IMF's own judgments; no independent check was found.

sudan-fuel-subsidy-removal-2021.whole: On 29 June 2021 Sudan reached the HIPC debt-relief 'decision point'. The IMF put the extra relief at US$23.3 billion in present-value terms (US$17.0 billion from other governments, US$4.6 billion from multilateral lenders, US$1.7 billion from commercial creditors), and projected Sudan's external debt to fall from about US$56 billion (163% of GDP) to US$6 billion (14% of GDP) once relief was complete. A new 39-month IMF loan arrangement was approved alongside. These are the IMF's projections, not results; no independent check was found.

By January 2013 inflation stood at 33%, while the IMF predicted 5.5% growth for 2013 (IRIN).

Mexico's real GDP fell 6.2% in 1995 and grew 5.2% in 1996; consumer inflation was 35% in 1995 and 34% in 1996, and real manufacturing earnings fell 13.5% in 1995 and another 11% in 1996. The US Treasury credits were fully repaid in January 1997 (Peterson Institute for International Economics), and all obligations under the package by 2000 (Yale Journal of Financial Crises).

conakry-water-lease.whole: In 1989 less than 40% of Conakry's people had piped water; by 1997 there were about 31,000 connections in Guinea, about 25,000 of them in Conakry, and the authors judged that coverage grew more slowly than planned and stayed low. Most people they spoke to agreed water and service quality improved sharply, and a 1994 study found Conakry's piped water met WHO drinking-water norms. Unaccounted-for water was still about 48% in 1996, bill collection from private customers fell from 75% in 1989-90 to around 60%, and the average tariff reached 880 Guinean francs per cubic metre by 1996, where the plan had foreseen 660 by 1995 (Ménard and Clarke, 2002). A World Bank working paper (Clarke, Ménard and Zuluaga, 2000) found most indicators improved but named illegal connections, poor collection and high prices as the main problems.

jordan-tax-protests-2018.whole: The 2016 IMF programme aimed to cut Jordan's public debt through tax and budget measures. By the IMF's 2020 review, budget cutting in 2016-17 'was significant but proved difficult to maintain during 2018-19': in 2019 growth was 2.0%, the deficit was 5.0% of GDP, government and guaranteed debt was 99.1% of GDP, and unemployment, not counting foreign workers, reached 19%, up from 18.5% in 2017. The IMF had said in 2019 that efforts to widen the tax base had 'fallen short of expectations', and the 2016 arrangement was followed by a new IMF financing arrangement in 2020. These are IMF figures; no independent check was found.

egypt-float-bread-protests-2017.whole: The IMF programme that required the float paid out SDR 8,596.57 million (about US$11.9 billion) by its end in July 2019, when the IMF said the 2% of GDP primary surplus target was met. By October 2019, The National reported from an IMF report and official statistics, general government debt had fallen from a peak of 103% of GDP in 2016/17 to an estimated 85%, urban inflation had fallen to 4.8%, its lowest in almost seven years, and unemployment was 7.5%, down from 12.9% in 2014/15. No poverty figures were given. These figures come from the IMF and the Egyptian government; no independent check was found.

ukraine-gas-heat-tariffs-2015.whole: By the IMF's 2017 review, Ukraine's inflation fell from a peak of 61% in April 2015 to 12.4% by end-2016, the economy grew 2.3% in 2016, and international reserves doubled to about US$15 billion. The overall deficit, including losses in the state energy sector, fell from 10% of GDP in 2014 to 2.3% in 2016. These are IMF figures; no independent check was found.

portugal-troika-austerity-2011.whole: Portugal left the 78-billion-euro EU-IMF programme in May 2014. Reuters reported then that unemployment had come down from a 2013 peak of 17.5% to 15% (nearly 800,000 people), that public debt was around 125% of GDP, and that labour costs had fallen 8% since 2011 (Eurostat), with wages down about 5% between 2010 and 2013 (European Commission). GDP fell 0.7% in the first quarter of 2014.

ireland-bailout-austerity-2010.whole: Ireland left its 85-billion-euro EU-IMF programme in December 2013, having met every major target, Reuters reported. Unemployment had fallen below 13% from a 15.1% peak in 2012, ten-year borrowing costs had dropped below 3.5% from a high of 15% early in the bailout, and total debt, at a peak of 124% of GDP in 2013, was projected to fall to 116% in 2014, with growth of about 2% forecast for 2014.

mongolia-eff-austerity-2017.whole: The 2017 package paired a three-year US$425 million IMF Extended Fund Facility with about US$5.5 billion in total official support. By the IMF's 2019 report, growth rose from 5.3% in 2017 to 6.9% in 2018, the primary budget balance went from a deficit of 11.2% of GDP in 2016 to a surplus of 5.9% in 2018, public debt fell to 73% of GDP at end-2018 from 87.6% in 2016, and gross reserves reached about US$3.5 billion. Only 5 of 11 scheduled reviews had been completed, with the sixth delayed. These are IMF figures; no independent check was found.

russia-mass-privatization-mortality.whole: By July 1994 about 41% of the roughly 240,000 enterprises Russia had at the start of the programme had been privatised; more than 20,000 joint-stock companies were created, shares in 16,500 were offered at voucher auctions, and by end-1994 there were about 40 million shareholders in the new companies or voucher funds. In spring 1994 the state's average remaining stake was no more than 17% (Radygin, OECD paper, 1996). A 1999 review by John Nellis in the IMF's Finance & Development found that managers and workers gained control of about two-thirds of the shares on average, and that in Russia and some other former Soviet economies and Mongolia, private ownership often did not lead to restructuring.

kenya-health-user-fees-1989.whole: The fees were meant to raise money for public health services. A 1995 study in Health Policy and Planning (Mwabu, Mwanzia and Liambila) found the revenue from user fees covered 2.4% of the recurrent health budget. The outpatient fee was suspended in September 1990 and brought back gradually from 1991 with management changes; by 1993-94, fee revenue was estimated at 37% of non-staff spending at provincial general hospitals, about a third of it from national insurance claims (study abstract, 'The fall and rise of cost sharing in Kenya').

zimbabwe-esap-health-school-fees.whole: The World Bank's own evaluation office (2004) found GDP grew an average 2.9% a year over 1991-97 (4.9% leaving out the 1992 drought year). Central government deficits averaged 8.8% of GDP over 1991-97 despite planned spending cuts, and domestic debt rose from 30% to 47% of GDP between 1990-91 and 1995-96. Extreme poverty rose from 26% to 35% of people between 1991 and 1995. The evaluation rated the outcome of Bank assistance in the 1990s 'unsatisfactory', the first adjustment credit moderately satisfactory and the second unsatisfactory. This is the World Bank's own evaluation office; no independent check was found.

ebola-imf-wage-limits.whole: In its December 2014 reply to the Lancet authors' criticism, the IMF said health spending as a share of GDP rose between 2010 and 2013 under its programmes: by 0.7 percentage points in Guinea, 1.6 in Liberia and 0.24 in Sierra Leone. It said it had made an additional US$130 million available to the three countries to fight Ebola and was working on ways to give more debt relief. malawi-november-2023-devaluation.whole: The four-year US$175 million IMF Extended Credit Facility paid out only its first US$35 million and ended in May 2025 with no review completed in 18 months; the IMF said it was not able to restore economic stability, citing spending pressures, weak revenue and a foreign-exchange system that made it hard to rebuild reserves (Reuters via TimesLIVE). The IMF confirmed the arrangement ended on 14 May 2025. By its July 2025 figures, growth fell to 1.8% in 2024, inflation peaked at 30.7% in February 2024 and was 27.7% in May 2025, the FY2024/25 deficit was 10.1% of GDP, public debt was about 88% of GDP at end-2024, and its table put gross reserves at US$118 million for 2025. The official kwacha rate had been fixed against the dollar since April 2024.

ethiopia-birr-float-2024.whole: Ethiopia's four-year IMF Extended Credit Facility, approved in July 2024, is for about US$3.4 billion, of which about US$2.183 billion had been paid out by January 2026. By the IMF's count, average inflation fell from 32.5% in 2022/23 to 16.0% in 2024/25, growth rose from 7.2% to 9.2%, reserves rose from 0.5 to 2.2 months of imports, and government revenue rose from 7.9% to 10.5% of GDP. The IMF said the government's own spending on targeted safety nets was below target, to make room for donor contributions. These are IMF figures; no independent check was found.

ghana-ecf-2023-tariffs-vat.whole: Ghana's US$3 billion IMF Extended Credit Facility, approved in May 2023, had paid out about US$2.8 billion by December 2025. By the IMF's count, growth was 3.1% in 2023, 5.7% in 2024 and a projected 4.8% in 2025; public debt fell from 79.1% of GDP in 2023 to 56.6% in 2025; gross reserves rose from US$3.66 billion to US$8.63 billion; and inflation came back within the Bank of Ghana's target range for the first time since 2021. The IMF gave no figure for the energy-sector shortfall the tariff rises were meant to close. These are IMF figures; no independent check was found.

argentina-imf-standby-2018.whole: The 2018 stand-by, raised in October 2018 to US$57 billion, was the largest in IMF history. The IMF's own ex-post evaluation (December 2021) concluded it 'did not fulfil the objectives of restoring confidence in fiscal and external viability': the programme went off track in August 2019, only four of 12 planned reviews were completed, and it was cancelled in July 2020. The evaluation said capital flight by residents and continued peso depreciation raised inflation and the peso value of public debt and weakened real incomes, 'especially of the poor'. Argentina's debt to the IMF then exceeded US$44 billion (Buenos Aires Times). This is the IMF's own evaluation; no independent check was found.

thailand-imf-1997-closures.whole: Thailand completed its 34-month IMF stand-by arrangement on 19 June 2000. By the IMF's count, real GDP fell 10.8% in 1998, grew 4.2% in 1999 and was expected to approach 5% in 2000; inflation was 0.7% at end-1999 and gross reserves reached US$34.8 billion. The IMF gave no unemployment or poverty figures and pointed to slow resolution of bad bank loans. These are IMF figures; no independent check was found.

xiaolangdi-resettlement.whole: The World Bank's Independent Evaluation Group (2007) found the dam gave flood protection to Henan and Shandong downstream, halted sediment build-up along the 800 km lower Yellow River, and regulated water supply to several cities and industrial centres. Hydropower generation exceeded appraisal estimates, while irrigation supply improved but stayed below target. Total cost at closing was US$2,688.8 million, and the economic rate of return was 13% against 20% expected at appraisal; IEG rated both phases 'highly satisfactory'. This is the World Bank's own evaluation office; no independent check was found.

upper-indravati-oustees.whole: The Upper Indravati power station has 600 MW of capacity in four 150 MW units; the first two were commissioned in 1999 and the others in 2000 and 2001, and the operator, Odisha Hydro Power Corporation, says the project irrigates more than 100,000 hectares (company figures). An ex-post evaluation by Japan's JBIC (field survey July 2003) of the part it funded found that irrigation component was completed in December 1998 at 55.7% of its planned yen cost, with a revised command area of 47,185 hectares. No independent figures on electricity generated were found.

pantabangan-dam-resettlement.whole: Pantabangan Dam was completed in 1974. It irrigates on average 87,300 hectares in the wet season and 82,500 hectares in the dry season, according to the manager of the Upper Pampanga River Integrated Irrigation Systems (Philippine Daily Inquirer). For the 2023 wet season the irrigation agency programmed 146,202 hectares and had irrigated 72,618 hectares in parts of Nueva Ecija and nearby provinces by 26 June (Philippine News Agency). These figures come from the government irrigation agency; no independent check of them, or figures on rice output or power generated, was found.

zambia-donegal-vulture-fund.whole: The debt began as a 1979 loan from Romania, mainly for Zambia to buy farming equipment. A BBC report puts the loan at US$15 million; a Council of Europe report gives US$15 million in its summary and US$30 million in its explanatory memorandum. Donegal bought it in 1999 for US$3.3 million (Council of Europe) and sought US$55 million. The London High Court found Zambia owed about US$15 million, and the final sum after interest and earlier payments was about US$15.5 million (BBC), which the Council of Europe gives as US$15.7 million. Zambia had US$1.92 billion of debt cancelled by the Paris Club in 2005 (Council of Europe).
